summary: The National Prescribed Fire Act of 2025 directs the Department of Agriculture and the Department of the Interior to increase the use of prescribed fires on federal lands over a 10-year period. It establishes programs, funding mechanisms, workforce support, training centers, and cooperative agreements with non-federal entities and Indian Tribes to carry out planned burns while coordinating with air quality agencies to manage public health risks from smoke.

affected_groups.effect: Receive potential hazard pay when performing prescribed fire ignition and control work, access to new training programs, and opportunities for permanent conversion from seasonal status.

Eligible to enter cooperative agreements and contracts, receive grants and financial assistance, participate in task forces, and collaborate on landscape-scale prescribed fire and smoke management programs.
Provided career pathways, training, and wraparound support to work as prescribed fire practitioners, including dedicated veteran crews.
Can receive federal contracts, grants, and liability protections equivalent to federal employees under the Federal Tort Claims Act while participating in approved prescribed fire activities.
affected_groups.group: Non-Federal Prescribed Fire Cooperators and Private Entities

key_provisions: Beginning in the first fiscal year after enactment and for 9 years following, the total acreage of federal land where prescribed fires are conducted must increase by at least 10 percent each year compared to the previous year.

The Secretary of Agriculture and the Secretary of the Interior may use up to 15 percent of annual appropriations for hazardous fuels management to fund prescribed fire activities, grants, training, and cooperative agreements.
Establishment of a Collaborative Prescribed Fire Program to select and fund large-scale landscape restoration and prescribed fire projects up to $1,000,000 per project annually.

Authorization for the Secretaries to enter into cooperative agreements or contracts of up to 10 years with states, Indian Tribes, local governments, fire districts, NGOs, and private entities to conduct prescribed fires on federal land.

Workforce enhancements including hazard pay for federal employees performing prescribed fire work, conversion of eligible seasonal firefighters to permanent status, career pathways for veterans and formerly incarcerated individuals, and the establishment of new training centers and an Indigenous-led training center.
Extension of Federal Tort Claims Act liability protections to non-federal cooperators acting under direct federal supervision during prescribed fire activities.

Coordination between the Environmental Protection Agency and state, tribal, and local air quality agencies to support smoke management, research, and exceptional event demonstrations for air quality standards.
missing_information: Exact total dollar amounts of annual appropriations for hazardous fuels management that will be subject to the 15 percent funding cap are not specified in the text.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The National Prescribed Fire Act of 2025 directs the Department of Agriculture and the Department of the Interior to increase the use of prescribed fires on federal lands over a 10-year period. It establishes programs, funding mechanisms, workforce support, training centers, and cooperative agreements with non-federal entities and Indian Tribes to carry out planned burns while coordinating with air quality agencies to manage public health risks from smoke.
summary_detail.significance: The bill mandates a systematic, compounding expansion of prescribed fire acreage on federal lands by 10 percent annually over a decade, supported by dedicated funding flexibility, multi-party task forces, and liability protections. It extensively alters federal coordination with state, local, tribal, and private partners to scale up hazardous fuels reduction and ecological restoration.

title: National Prescribed Fire Act of 2025
